ScientificMethodIdentity checks that the catalog-entry schema name agrees with the catalog ID. It does not load a trusted catalog or verify the recorded origin, regime, maturity, completeness, availability, or digest. A consumer must compare the record with a trusted catalog snapshot.

Split checks bind membership, parent-row-ledger, and partition-manifest identities. They do not read the manifest or member lists. They do not prove that members belong to the parent ledger, that splits are disjoint, or that the splits cover the parent rows.

ScientificOutcomeCoverageValidator accepts checked Rust reports for one exact ledger. It rejects a different ledger and duplicate outcome IDs before mutation. Finalization requires one terminal report for every ledger entry. It records request, status, support, preflight, and estimation counts. This request-ledger coverage is not statistical interval coverage.

The coverage validator accepts at most 1024 ledger entries. For a complete accepted set, full-ledger equality contributes at most 1048576 entry-equality checks. Outcome-ID lookup adds bounded logarithmic work for each report. A larger contract needs detached ledger references. The cap is not caller-adjustable in this contract revision.

The coverage validator is not an external event-stream validator. It does not require a ledger event before outcomes. Failed reports do not contribute. Successful accepted sets are order-independent, but error selection for an invalid sequence can depend on input order.
